title: Fix the Bug: Always-True Range Check
hints: Every integer is either greater than 20 **or** less than 39 — so `||` is always true.
"Between" means both conditions must hold. Or ask a range whether it contains the value.
`(21...38).contains(temp)` — and return the condition directly instead of `if … return true`.
jsBridge: The classic `x > 20 || x < 39` bug is language-agnostic. Swift gives you `(21...38).contains(x)` or `21...38 ~= x`, which states the intent. Pattern matching on ranges (`case 21...38:`) is the same operator.

compass.q: `range.contains(x)` vs `range ~= x` vs `case range:`: are they the same operation?
JS has no range literals. How would you make this bug impossible there? Is a helper function as good?
"Strictly between" vs "between inclusive": how do `20<..<39` style ranges not exist in Swift, and what do you write instead?
Validation rules (age, password length) often hide boundary bugs. How would you table-test them in XCTest or Swift Testing?
